# Variable Interpolation in PHP Heredocs: The `<<<` Syntax Rules A common stumbling block for developers moving from simple string concatenation to multi-line strings is the behavior of heredocs regarding variables. If you attempt to output dynamic data inside a heredoc without adjusting the syntax, your variables will render as literal text rather than their evaluated values. This happens because PHP treats heredoc strings differently based on whether they are quoted or unquoted. In your specific case, the code fails because the heredoc delimiter is defined with single quotes: `<<<'EX'`. When you use single quotes in the opening tag following `<<<`, PHP enters a "literal" mode. In this mode, the parser treats everything between the opening and closing delimiters as plain text. It ignores variables like `$data['game_name']` and special characters like `<` or `>` (HTML entities), outputting them exactly as written. To get variable interpolation to work, you must remove the single quote from the delimiter tag.
